name: Burlywood
lede: Burlywood is a pale tan from the X11 and CSS color lists, found in about one painting in twenty in our archive.

sections.title: A tan in the web list
sections.body:
Paterson calls BurlyWood a tan colour and one of the colours in the X11 Color Set, with hex code #DEB887 [1]. It is also a CSS keyword [3]. The dictionary does not explain the name, and its origin is undocumented here [1].

The library finds the same name in the Maerz and Paul dictionary, first recorded in 1912, and in the ISCC-NBS lists of 1955 [3]. Nearby names are [[tan]], [[wheat]], [[khaki]] and [[sandy-brown]] [3]. The hex value is a screen approximation of a tan, not a measured pigment [1][3]. In LCH terms it measures lightness 77, chroma 31 and hue 77 degrees, and its nearest library name is Tan [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this tan in 1,154 of 23,531 paintings, about 4.9 percent, as photographed [2]. John Singer Sargent has it in 27 paintings and Mughal paintings in 56 [2]. Measured values are screen approximations of varnished canvases [2]. The count is a computed color match, not an identification of any pigment [2].
